pitch: Exploit high-bandwidth RAM across many Cloudflare Edge Workers: explode a dataset too large for one machine into per-worker memory, run SIMD/MIMD-style anomaly detection and incremental training across workers, and persist only the deltas -- so a model can be trained on data that would not fit in one machine's memory. Target: live in 30 days.

tasks.title: Run end-to-end at target scale
tasks.duration_basis: The first point every prior piece has to actually work together, not just in isolation -- classic integration-day risk, where the pessimistic case is one full extra debugging pass.

tasks.title: Deploy and launch
tasks.duration_basis: The launch gate itself; pessimistic case is a rollback dry run or secrets/limits review turning up something that has to be fixed before go-live.

tasks.title: Choose a streaming-friendly anomaly algorithm
tasks.duration_basis: Same calendar risk as any decision task, compounded by a real technical trade-off (streaming z-score/IQR vs. online isolation-forest vs. sketch-based) that has to actually be presented, not just asked.

tasks.title: Measure the per-invocation compute budget
tasks.duration_basis: A representative chunk is hard to pick before the real loader exists; the pessimistic case is faking one, getting an unrepresentative number, and having to redo it once ingest-loader lands.

tasks.title: Validate accuracy against a single-machine baseline
tasks.duration_basis: An unfavorable accuracy gap sends this back to kernel-algo for a second pass, not just a longer benchmark run -- the pessimistic case is one round-trip through that loop.

tasks.title: Build and benchmark the SIMD kernel
tasks.duration_basis: The single most novel, highest-skill-risk build in the plan -- WASM SIMD tuning has a long, unpredictable tail even for an experienced engineer.

tasks.title: Size the per-worker chunk
tasks.duration_basis: Only decidable once both upstream measurements land cleanly; if either was ambiguous this negotiation drags while a second measurement is sought.

tasks.title: Build the shard loader
tasks.duration_basis: First real implementation on the critical path; typical first-integration slip once the measured ceilings turn out tighter in practice than in a spike.

tasks.title: Measure worker-to-worker transfer
tasks.duration_basis: Optimistic: the docs already settle it -- no shared-memory primitive exists, confirmed and done. Pessimistic: this is the pitch's central claim, so it's worth trying several near-misses (SharedArrayBuffer, a KV race, a Durable Object as a mailbox) before writing down a confident 'no'.

tasks.title: Choose the coordination primitive
tasks.duration_basis: A real architecture decision with cost/latency trade-offs; same calendar risk as other decision tasks.

tasks.title: Define the delta format
tasks.duration_basis: A narrower decision than most here (format follows from the primitive already chosen), so the tail is shorter.

tasks.title: Define the reduce step
tasks.duration_basis: Ordering/dedupe guarantees are subtle and easy to under-scope on a first pass; pessimistic case is a second design pass once a gap is noticed.

tasks.title: Build dispatch and collect
tasks.duration_basis: The first real exercise of the platform's true concurrency ceiling rather than an assumed one -- likely to surface surprises the fan-out spike didn't catch.

tasks.title: Build state accumulation and reload
tasks.duration_basis: Concurrent-writer correctness is the plan's one stated coverage gap (see sys-train's covers_why below); this is where it actually has to get solved in code, which is where estimates most often blow out.

tasks.title: Handle worker failure
tasks.duration_basis: Absent from the original pitch, so there's no prior design to build against -- real risk of discovering a second failure mode mid-implementation.

tasks.title: Confirm the model supports incremental updates
tasks.duration_basis: If no online variant is documented for the chosen algorithm, this stops being a lookup and becomes its own small research task.

tasks.title: Add per-pass observability
tasks.duration_basis: Mostly wiring against metrics that already exist elsewhere in the build; modest tail.

tasks.title: Measure the per-isolate memory ceiling
tasks.duration_basis: Optimistic: the kill signal is unambiguous and the ceiling is read off in one run. Pessimistic: the kill is a CPU-time limit, not a memory limit, and the measurement has to be redesigned to isolate the real cause.

tasks.title: Confirm WASM SIMD availability
tasks.duration_basis: Low-stakes docs lookup either way; the only slippage risk is the docs being unclear about which runtime version ships the proposal.

tasks.title: Measure concurrency and fan-out ceilings
tasks.duration_basis: Pessimistic: the real ceiling is plan-tier-dependent and undocumented for the exact combination needed, so it may take a support ticket rather than a self-serve measurement.

tasks.title: Measure exchange bandwidth and price
tasks.duration_basis: Two separate channels to benchmark (R2, Durable Objects), each with its own time-of-day variance; pessimistic case is re-running both to get a stable figure.

tasks.title: Choose where the source dataset lives
tasks.duration_basis: Optimistic: a same-day call once the trade-off is laid out. Pessimistic: this needs the user's calendar, not more analysis -- decision tasks slip on availability, not difficulty.

tasks.title: Choose where accumulating state lives
tasks.duration_basis: A consequential choice with a real consistency/latency trade-off; same calendar risk as other decision tasks.

tasks.title: Build a real cost projection
tasks.duration_basis: Depends on three upstream measurements; if any came in worse than assumed, the cost model has to be redone before it's a stated figure.
